sowhat.text: Stock-funded tech deals get harder when buyers' shares fall, as Marvell and Lumentum both dropped on their $115B deal. Infrastructure money keeps flowing, with Blackstone and Canadian pensions paying $3.1B into LNG Canada, and a December hike (about 76%) keeps debt costly.

pitch: Stocks were mixed Monday. The S&P 500 fell half a percent to about 7,541 and the Nasdaq fell 1.1% as the AI sell-off continued, while the Dow rose 0.4%. Oil dropped about 7%, with WTI at 96 dollars, on hopes of a US-Iran deal. The 10-year eased to 4.91%, and the market puts about a 76% chance on a Fed hike on December 9. On deals, Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum for about 115 billion dollars in stock, and Blackstone and Canadian pensions are paying 3.1 billion dollars into LNG Canada. Credit spreads, last read Friday, were wider but still open for deals.

quiz.q: Where did WTI crude settle on Monday 2 Nov, and how far did it fall?
quiz.a: $96.46, down about 7.4%, on hopes of a US-Iran deal.

quiz.q: Why did oil fall about 7% on Monday?
quiz.a: Hopes that the US and Iran would keep negotiating rather than escalate. Traders priced in a possible deal, and Brent settled at $104.77 and WTI at $96.46.

quiz.q: Who advised Lumentum on its sale to Marvell?
quiz.a: Citi and Evercore advised Lumentum (Davis Polk was legal counsel). Qatalyst, J.P. Morgan and Goldman Sachs advised Marvell.

chat.a: Mixed day on Monday: the S&P 500 fell 0.5% to 7,541 and the Nasdaq fell 1.1% as the AI sell-off continued, while the Dow rose 0.4%. Oil dropped about 7% on US-Iran talk hopes. For bankers, the question is whether weaker tech stock currency slows stock-funded deals.
chat.tip: Lead with the split between tech and the Dow.

chat.q: What's your read on oil this week?
chat.a: WTI settled at $96.46, down 7.4%, and Brent at $104.77, down 7.6%, on hopes of a US-Iran deal. That can reverse on any headline. Lower oil trims energy cash flow, which could slow energy capex and deals if it holds.
chat.tip: Say both directions: deal hopes down, supply scares up.

chat.a: Marvell is buying Lumentum for about $115B in stock at a roughly 24% premium, with Qatalyst, J.P. Morgan and Goldman on Marvell and Citi and Evercore on Lumentum. Blackstone and Canadian pensions are also paying $3.1B for 49.9% of Mitsubishi's holding company for its LNG Canada stake.
chat.tip: Name the advisers; bankers will ask.

chat.q: What are you watching this week?
chat.a: The October jobs report on Friday 6 Nov, about +55K expected with unemployment at 4.2%, because it feeds the odds of a Fed hike on 9 Dec, near 76% now. Also earnings from ConocoPhillips and Parker-Hannifin on Thursday as reads on energy and industrial demand.
chat.tip: Tie each event to the Fed or the energy theme.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: The 10-year is 4.91% now. A 50 bp rise lifts the risk-free rate and so the WACC, which lowers the present value of cash flows. Long-duration companies with most value in the terminal value fall the most.
chat.tip: Say the direction, then who is hit hardest.

chat.q: How would a tech sell-off change M&A activity?
chat.a: The Nasdaq fell 1.1%, and Marvell fell almost 13% after announcing its all-stock Lumentum deal. Falling shares make stock currency less attractive and can reprice tech targets. Buyers lean toward cash deals and hard assets, such as the LNG Canada stake.
chat.tip: Separate stock-funded deals from cash deals.

chat.q: How do the Fed and the 10-year affect M&A financing right now?
chat.a: The Fed target is 3.75–4.00% after a 25 bp hike in September, and futures price about a 76% chance of another on 9 Dec. The 10-year is 4.91%, so debt is costly. High yield spreads were 344 bp on Friday, wider but still open to borrowers.
chat.tip: Separate the base rate from the credit spread.
